finding_title: FeeTaker is not accounting for unwrapWeth Feature
purpose: Two-side PoC for a V3.1 patch candidate: the same fill scenario, adapted to each revision's interfaces, executed on both recorded revisions. Violation only on the vulnerable side.

commands.setup: git worktree add <dir> <revision>; npm install (the tree ships no lockfile, so npm ci is unavailable)

scenario: fillOrderArgs on an order with makerTraits.unwrapWeth = true, takerAsset = WETH, order.receiver = FeeTaker, postInteraction fee in extraData; without msg.value (the protocol pulls WETH, withdraws it and sends ETH to the receiver).

vulnerable.failure: the M-01 scenario reverts without a reason string at OrderMixin._fill (contracts/OrderMixin.sol:423): _WETH.safeWithdrawTo sends ETH to order.getReceiver() (the FeeTaker), which has no receive()/fallback at this revision

fixed.note: includes the two ETH-fee tests added by the fix commit; the fix adds receive() and an ETH branch to postInteraction

results.controls: the four non-unwrapWeth fee-flow tests pass on both revisions; only the unwrapWeth ETH scenario separates them

conclusion: The observed failure is exactly the M-01 mechanism (review scope: limit-order-protocol), and it is absent on the recorded fix revision. This flips the finding's review-layer fix_effectiveness to effective under the two-side rule; the frozen V3.1 candidate record stays untouched.
caveats: hardhat 2.19.4 prints a Node.js 24 unsupported-version warning on every command; both suites nevertheless compile and run deterministically (outputs in the logs)

the adapted test is the fix commit's own ETH-fee test carried back to the vulnerable revision's interfaces (parameterless constructor, uint24/1e7 extraData encoding); the four pre-existing tests are unchanged
the two revisions also carry unrelated FeeTaker changes (uint16/1e5 fee encoding, onlyLimitOrderProtocol, rescueFunds); the PoC isolates the ETH path, not those
